subject: Recap: Redwood demo + procurement & security next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Redwood demo + procurement & security next steps

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time to run through the Redwood demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- What we covered: demo of dedicated vs hosted inference, predictable latency targets, cost controls (batching + quantization), and RBAC/audit features relevant to Acme's environment.
- Procurement signals from call: you mentioned Procurement prefers PO for SaaS buys, and there's potential interest in AWS Marketplace if that speeds procurement.
- Security gating: you asked about SOC 2, DPA, and whether we can complete Acme's security questionnaire as part of qualification.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will share our SOC 2 Type II report + standard DPA for review (attached).
2) Aditya (SE) will review the Acme security questionnaire and provide answers/notes for technical items.
3) Please confirm the procurement contact and whether Acme prefers a PO (net terms) or AWS Marketplace billing — either works, just different paperwork/timeline. If PO, we can route a quote + MSA/SOW to Procurement; if Marketplace, we can provide the marketplace listing + instructions.
4) I'll open a DocuSign quote for the initial committed capacity once commercial path is confirmed.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_2025.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v2.1.pdf

Open items for Acme: procurement contact, preferred billing path (PO vs Marketplace), and any high-priority security questionnaire sections we should prioritize.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference
https://www.redwoodinference.com

From: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood demo + procurement & security next steps

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. A few quick answers from Procurement side:

- We generally prefer to pay via PO with net 30 terms. Procurement is the canonical owner for contract review (procurement@acme.com).
- There is interest in AWS Marketplace if it reduces legal review time, but Procurement will still expect standard DPA language.
- Can you confirm if your SOC 2 report includes any customer-scoped controls for data residency/audit logs? That will be a gating item for our security team.

I've cc'd Procurement so they see the attachments. They may push back if the DPA needs edits.

Thanks —
Jamie Rogers
Product Lead, AI Platform | Acme Corporation
jamie.rogers@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood demo + procurement & security next steps

Thanks Jamie — good to know. Quick clarifications: 

- SOC 2 Type II (attached) covers our control environment for hosting and access controls; we include audit logging and retention practices in the report. For data residency, we support region controls for customer data in Dedicated/Private deployments — if you're evaluating hosted, we can document region options and retention policies.
- DPA: attached is our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.1.pdf). We're open to reasonable edits but do need to preserve certain security and crypto controls.
- Marketplace vs PO: two paths
   * PO (Net 30): we'll send a quote + MSA/SOW. Dev, can you draft the quote and DocuSign envelope once Procurement confirms exact billing contact and PO reference format?
   * AWS Marketplace: faster procurement, but may require marketplace-specific billing and limits on contract edits. If this is preferred, please confirm and we'll send the marketplace listing and steps.

Aditya — can you take the attached Acme questionnaire and return a filled version with any flagged items?

Procurement team — when convenient, please share the contact and PO template (if any) so Dev can include the correct fields on the quote.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood demo + procurement & security next steps

Hi all —

I've started working through the Acme security questionnaire (attached). A few notes from an SE perspective: 

- Timeline: we can return a majority of the questionnaire within 3 business days; items requiring legal/SaaS architecture details (DPA edits or custom residency commitments) may take longer.
- Audit logs & residency: hosted customers get detailed audit logs (per-route, token-level) and log export; if Acme needs a dedicated region or on-prem bundle, that would be scoped as Dedicated/Private and is part of the Dedicated procurement path.
- Dependencies: I'll flag items where we need Procurement/legal sign-off (e.g., encryption key custody (KMS/HSM) or custom data residency SLAs).

Attached: acme_security_questionnaire_filled_by_redwood.xlsx (partial — marked sections need Acme input).

Happy to jump on a short call with your security team if that helps accelerate answers.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood demo + procurement & security next steps

Hi Procurement team —

Thanks for looping in. Per Marissa's note, here are the practical options from a commercial operations perspective: 

1) PO (Net 30) path — typical timeline: 7-14 business days once Procurement confirms contact + PO format. Deliverables from us: quote (line-item capacity), MSA (standard), and SOW if you want to lock specific throughput/SLAs. We'll send via DocuSign (link to preview: https://docusign.com/rwd/acme-quote-045).

2) AWS Marketplace — can be faster for procurement but may require marketplace-specific billing and limits on contract edits. If this is preferred, please confirm and we'll send the marketplace listing and steps.

Please confirm the following so I can prepare the right paperwork:
- Full procurement contact name + email
- PO reference format (e.g., ACME-PO-12345)
- Preferred billing path (PO vs AWS Marketplace)

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
